rationale: The prompt requests channels where a workspace admin is a member, author, or reactor; resolution_mode multiple matches the plural 'channels' request, and referent CONVERSATION with route through WORKSPACE/WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP is faithfully used to filter by the admin's direct connection. Cross-checking base_seed: only U03ROBERT23 (admin) touches channels, and exactly the three cited channels (general, random, engineering) via membership/authorship — verified against channel_members and messages with no missed or extra matches. U07MORGANFREE (the other admin) appears in no channel_members/messages/reactions, correctly supporting the uninvolved_admin negative. The namesake U_ROBERT (Robert Chen) has workspace role 'member' (not admin) and appears in project-alpha-dev and several other channels (core-infra, model-research, product-growth, frontend) — none of which are wrongly included, correctly demonstrating the role-split negative. The no-admin channel (growth) is confirmed to contain only plain-member participants. Remaining seeded channels (C_INFRA, C_MODEL, C_GROWTH, C_FRONTEND, D01AGENTSOPHIE, C05ALPHA, C_OLD_PROJECT) were checked and contain no admin touches, so the match set is complete without hidden omissions or extra unintended matches. The access_plan realistically composes conversations.list/members/history plus reactions.get per message and users.info for role lookup, consistent with the documented API surface and runtime_qualifications. Answer attributes are bare channels.channel_name/channel_id columns. The binding_note adds a legitimate, requested-consistent disambiguation (same-person role join) rather than a secretly imposed condition. Negatives are well-chosen and non-trivial (uninvolved admin, namesake with mismatched role, admin-absent channel), giving a strong, well-calibrated case.
